g.text: How a Tailscale connection really starts: relay first, then upgrade
Not "try direct, then fall back": DERP is the bootstrap path while direct paths are probed.
ping best path every 3 s while
Which path carries the packets over time:
DERP stays available as the fallback
Every minute Tailscale tries again for a better direct path. If NO path ever answers (hard NAT on both sides, UDP blocked),
traffic simply stays on DERP: slower, but it works. `tailscale status` shows "active; direct <addr>" or "active; relay <region>".
